{
  "case_orientation": "This Supreme Court of Canada decision addresses whether, under s. 34(1)(e) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA), a finding of inadmissibility for 'engaging in acts of violence that would or might endanger the lives or safety of persons in Canada' requires a nexus to national security or the security of Canada. The case reviews administrative decisions (Immigration Appeal Division and Immigration Division), Federal Court, and Federal Court of Appeal, focusing on the appropriate standard of review (reasonableness vs. correctness) for certified questions under s. 74(d) IRPA. The majority holds that reasonableness is the standard, but finds the administrative interpretations unreasonable for failing to consider statutory context and international law constraints. The minority (Côté J.) would apply correctness review to certified questions. The appeals are allowed, the administrative decisions are quashed, and the applicants' inadmissibility findings are set aside. (See paras. 1–12, 54, 121–123, 124–127, 189; citation_ids: 7658399, 7658403, 7658411, 7658414, 7658415, 7658509, 7658511, 7658513, 7658514, 7658528, 7658529, 7658532, 7658535, 7658536, 7658539.)",
